text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A delegation of Russian MPs began a visit to Latvia. Parliament speaker Alfred Chepanis said the Duma deputies spent most of the time speaking about the situation of the Russian speakers in Latvia, most of whom do not have citizenship. He said they threatened both economic and political sanctions unless the situation improved.
- The finance ministry has agreed to boost budget spending by 26 million lats as ministries and other public institutues ask for 34 million lats.
- Customs have seized four cargos of illegal alchohol recently.
- The cabinet committee approved a rise in the capital of the central bank to 25 million lats from 2.5 million lats.
- The newspaper's correspondents in Moscow and Belarus report on the building of a radar station near Baranovichi in Belarus to replace the old Soviet monitoring station at Skrunda in Latvia.
- A 4.1 million Ecu loan will be made available for Latvia by EU PHARE to improve transport infrastructure.
- The newspaper says there is no sign of the thaw in relations with Moscow promised by some Latvian politicians.
- Ventspils Nafta shareholders on April 30 discussed a draft report on the company's activities in 1996 and approved last year's draft budget.
- Businessmen, state officials and customs experts have expressed their dissastisfaction with a new customs law.
